label: Acts 22:1
text: “Brothers and fathers, listen to the defense which I now make to you.”

label: Acts 22:2
text: When they heard that he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, they were even more quiet. He said,

label: Acts 22:3
text: “I am indeed a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, instructed according to the strict tradition of the law of our fathers, being zealous for God, even as you all are today.

label: Acts 22:4
text: I persecuted this Way to the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.

label: Acts 22:5
text: As also the high priest and all the council of the elders testify, from whom also I received letters to the brothers, and traveled to Damascus to bring them also who were there to Jerusalem in bonds to be punished.

label: Acts 22:6
text: As I made my journey, and came close to Damascus, about noon, suddenly a great light shone around me from the sky.

label: Acts 22:7
text:
I fell to the ground, and heard a voice saying to me,
‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?’

label: Acts 22:8
text:
I answered, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ He said to me,
‘I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you persecute.’

label: Acts 22:9
text: “Those who were with me indeed saw the light and were afraid, but they didn’t understand the voice of him who spoke to me.

label: Acts 22:10
text:
I said, ‘What shall I do, Lord?’ The Lord said to me,
‘Arise, and go into Damascus. There you will be told about all things which are appointed for you to do.’

label: Acts 22:11
text: When I couldn’t see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of those who were with me, I came into Damascus.

label: Acts 22:12
text: One Ananias, a devout man according to the law, well reported of by all the Jews who lived in Damascus,

label: Acts 22:13
text: came to me, and standing by me said to me, ‘Brother Saul, receive your sight!’ In that very hour I looked up at him.

label: Acts 22:14
text: He said, ‘The God of our fathers has appointed you to know his will, and to see the Righteous One, and to hear a voice from his mouth.

label: Acts 22:15
text: For you will be a witness for him to all men of what you have seen and heard.

label: Acts 22:16
text: Now why do you wait? Arise, be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling on the name of the Lord.’

label: Acts 22:17
text: “When I had returned to Jerusalem, and while I prayed in the temple, I fell into a trance,

label: Acts 22:18
text:
and saw him saying to me,
‘Hurry and get out of Jerusalem quickly, because they will not receive testimony concerning me from you.’

label: Acts 22:19
text: I said, ‘Lord, they themselves know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue those who believed in you.

label: Acts 22:20
text: When the blood of Stephen, your witness, was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting to his death, and guarding the cloaks of those who killed him.’

label: Acts 22:21
text:
“He said to me,
‘Depart, for I will send you out far from here to the Gentiles.’”

label: Acts 22:22
text: They listened to him until he said that; then they lifted up their voice, and said, “Rid the earth of this fellow, for he isn’t fit to live!”

label: Acts 22:23
text: As they cried out, and threw off their cloaks, and threw dust into the air,

label: Acts 22:24
text: the commanding officer commanded him to be brought into the barracks, ordering him to be examined by scourging, that he might know for what crime they shouted against him like that.

label: Acts 22:25
text: When they had tied him up with thongs, Paul asked the centurion who stood by, “Is it lawful for you to scourge a man who is a Roman, and not found guilty?”

label: Acts 22:26
text: When the centurion heard it, he went to the commanding officer and told him, “Watch what you are about to do, for this man is a Roman!”

label: Acts 22:27
text:
The commanding officer came and asked him, “Tell me, are you a Roman?”
He said, “Yes.”

label: Acts 22:28
text:
The commanding officer answered, “I bought my citizenship for a great price.”
Paul said, “But I was born a Roman.”

label: Acts 22:29
text: Immediately those who were about to examine him departed from him, and the commanding officer also was afraid when he realized that he was a Roman, because he had bound him.

label: Acts 22:30
text: But on the next day, desiring to know the truth about why he was accused by the Jews, he freed him from the bonds, and commanded the chief priests and all the council to come together, and brought Paul down and set him before them.

label: Paul addressed the Jerusalem crowd in the Hebrew (Aramaic) dialect, and the crowd kept even quieter
statement: Paul opened his defense to the crowd in the Hebrew language (hebraisti); when they heard that he spoke to them in the Hebrew language they were even more quiet.
note: Modern reference (source, not an evidence node): Aramaic was a common language of Roman Judaea, and 'the Hebrew dialect' is often interpreted as 'the (Aramaic) vernacular of the Jews' (fetched Wikipedia 'Language of Jesus'). Grade C for the language setting; the crowd's reaction is the narrative's own report.

label: Paul was brought up in Jerusalem at the feet of Gamaliel, trained in the strict tradition of the law
statement: Paul, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, was brought up in Jerusalem at the feet of Gamaliel, instructed according to the strict tradition of the law of our fathers, zealous for God.
note: The training under Gamaliel is Paul's own report; no external source names Paul as Gamaliel's pupil (none-found). Gamaliel the Elder himself is attested A by the rabbinic nodes reused from Acts 5 (Mishnah Sotah 9:15; Gittin 4:2-3).

label: Paul persecuted this Way to the death, binding and delivering both men and women to prison
statement: Paul persecuted this Way to the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.
note: Paul's persecutor role is his own report; Galatians 1:13 is a biblical cross-reference, not external evidence. None-found.

label: Paul's companions saw the light and were afraid, but did not understand the voice
statement: Those who were with Paul saw the light and were afraid, but did not understand the voice of him who spoke to him.
note: Acts 9:7 says the companions 'heard the sound but saw no one'; Acts 22:9 says they 'saw the light and were afraid, but did not understand the voice' - a long-noted discrepancy between the two retellings. Both are the narrative's own report; recorded as related_to, not complicates.

label: Ananias, a devout observer of the law, well reported of by all the Jews of Damascus, came to restore Paul's sight
statement: One Ananias, a devout man according to the law, well reported of by all the Jews who lived in Damascus, came, stood by Paul and said, 'Brother Saul, receive your sight!'
note: The same Damascus disciple as Acts 9:10 (related_to); Acts 22 adds his law-observance and good repute among the city's Jews. No external source names him.

label: Baptism washing away sins, calling on the name of the Lord
statement: Ananias told Paul: 'Arise, be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling on the name of the Lord.'
note: A theological instruction of the narrative; the baptismal custom itself is not externally attested for Damascus in the 30s CE. None-found.

label: In a trance in the temple Paul was told to leave Jerusalem and go far to the Gentiles
statement: When Paul had returned to Jerusalem and was praying in the temple, he fell into a trance; the Lord told him to hurry out of Jerusalem because they would not receive his testimony, and later, 'Depart, for I will send you out far from here to the Gentiles.'
note: Vision claim; none-found in every external category. Never graded from setting evidence.

label: The crowd shouted 'Rid the earth of this fellow!', threw off their cloaks and flung dust into the air
statement: At the mention of the Gentiles the crowd lifted up their voices, crying 'Rid the earth of this fellow, for he isn't fit to live!', waving their cloaks and throwing dust into the air.
note: The riot is the narrative's own report; the dust-throwing protest gesture has no external witness. None-found.

label: The tribune ordered Paul examined by scourging in the barracks
statement: The commanding officer (chiliarchos, tribune) had Paul brought into the barracks and ordered him examined by scourging, to learn for what crime they shouted against him; they tied him up with thongs.
note: Interrogation by scourging of an uncondemned prisoner, and the fortress barracks (the Antonia) as the tribune's headquarters, are the Roman setting; the event itself has no external witness.

label: Paul asked whether it was lawful to scourge a Roman citizen uncondemned
statement: Paul, tied with thongs, asked the centurion standing by: 'Is it lawful for you to scourge a man who is a Roman, and not found guilty?'
note: The same citizen protection Cicero invokes for In Verres 2.5 (reused graph node, grade B): scourging a Roman citizen is a wickedness under the Porcian laws.

label: The tribune was afraid when he learned Paul was a Roman, because he had bound him
statement: The centurion reported that Paul was a Roman; the tribune came, asked, and was afraid when he realized he was a Roman, because he had bound him; those about to examine him departed.
note: The fear presupposes the legal exposure of binding a citizen (Cicero, In Verres 2.5.66: 'It is a crime to bind a Roman citizen'). The event itself has no external witness.

label: The tribune said he had bought his Roman citizenship for a great price
statement: The commanding officer answered, 'I bought my citizenship for a great price.'
note: Cassius Dio 60.17.5-6 (reused text node): under Claudius the franchise was 'bought... from Messalina and the imperial freedmen', at first 'only for large sums' - the same practice and period (grade B). Paul's reply, 'But I was born a Roman', is his own report.

label: Paul said he was born a Roman citizen
statement: Paul replied to the tribune: 'But I was born a Roman.'
note: Paul's citizenship is his own report (22:25-29; 16:37-39); no external source attests that Paul held Roman citizenship by birth. None-found.

label: The tribune freed Paul from the bonds and summoned the chief priests and the whole council
statement: On the next day, wanting to know the truth of the accusation, the tribune freed Paul from the bonds, commanded the chief priests and all the council to come together, and brought Paul down and set him before them.
note: The Sanhedrin's assembly under a tribune's summons is the narrative's own report; none-found.

label: Cassius Dio, Roman History 60.17.5-7 (citizenship bought under Claudius)
author: Cassius Dio
note: Under Claudius many 'bought it from Messalina and the imperial freedmen'; the franchise was 'at first sold only for large sums' and was later so cheapened 'that a man could become a citizen by giving the right person some bits of broken glass' (60.17.5-6); informers accused new citizens of 'not adopting Claudius' name' (60.17.7).

label: LacusCurtius: Cassius Dio, Roman History Book 60
title: Cassius Dio, Roman History, Book 60 (Cary)
excerpt: many bought it from Messalina and the imperial freedmen. 6 For this reason, though the privilege was at first sold only for large sums, it later became so cheapened by the facility with which it could be obtained that it came to be a common saying

label: Wikipedia: Language of Jesus (Aramaic a common language of Roman Judaea)
title: Language of Jesus
excerpt: Aramaic was a common language of Roman Judaea , and was thus also spoken by at least some of Jesus' disciples .

label: Paul (Saul of Tarsus)
note: First mention at Acts 7:58 as the young man at whose feet the witnesses laid their garments; later Acts chapters reuse this node.

label: Gamaliel the Elder (Rabban Gamaliel I)
aka: Rabban Gamliel the Elder; grandson of Hillel
dates: a leading authority in the Sanhedrin in the early first century CE (fetched Wikipedia summary)

label: The Antonia Fortress (Herodian citadel at the Temple Mount's northwest corner)
periods: Hellenistic and Herodian origins; early Roman period

label: Wikipedia: Antonia Fortress
title: Antonia Fortress
excerpt: as a fortress whose chief function was to protect the Second Temple . It was built in Jerusalem at the eastern end of the Second Wall, at the north-western corner of the Temple Mount , and was connected to the Temple by porticoes .

label: Wikipedia: Antonia Fortress (Pilate's garrison next to the Temple mount at feast time)
title: Antonia Fortress
excerpt: During the greatest pilgrimage feast, when hundreds of thousands came to the Temple, Pilate likely had to be with his garrison next to the Temple mount as a potential focus of the uprising

author: Josephus

label: Cicero, In Verres 2.5 (the Porcian-law oration: 'I am a Roman citizen')
author: Marcus Tullius Cicero
note: The prosecution of Verres for scourging and crucifying Roman citizens in Sicily (73-70 BCE): 'It is a crime to bind a Roman citizen; to scourge him is a wickedness; to put him to death is almost parricide' (2.5.66); 'O Porcian law!' (2.5.63). Older editions number the same passage Book 5, chapters 161-170.
